description: Tanod: origin workload governor. Panels are ordered by the question an operator actually asks, health first. Every metric here is labelled only by config-derived values — route id, upstream address, limiter name — never by anything a client controls.

panels.title: Instances draining
panels.description: Readiness answers 503 while an instance drains, and it keeps serving normally throughout. Non-zero is expected during a deploy; non-zero for longer than a deploy means one was withdrawn and never replaced.

panels.title: Healthy upstreams
panels.description: Backends passing their health check, across the fleet. Zero does not stop Tanod serving — refusing to pick would turn a degraded origin into a guaranteed outage — but it means users are on stale_if_error.

panels.title: Configs in force
panels.description: Distinct effective-configuration fingerprints across the fleet. More than one means replicas do not agree, regardless of restart or reload counts.

panels.title: Origin work avoided
panels.description: Of the requests the cache could have answered, the share it did (hit or stale). Numerator and denominator both come from tanod_cache_total, so the value stays between 0 and 100%. (tanod_reuse_eligible_requests_total is counted at a different point and can disagree with it.)

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: Everything arriving at the traffic listener, served or shed.

panels.title: Origin load — is the ceiling holding, and is it the right one?
Origin work in flight vs the ceiling
panels.description: Both series are a count of permits, so they share one axis. In flight pinned at the limit means saturated: check render latency before raising the ceiling, because a higher ceiling against a slower origin makes it slower still.

panels.title: Admission decisions
panels.description: Shedding is the mechanism working and users receiving 503 at the same time. Both readings are true; act on the origin, not on the proxy.

panels.title: Origin render latency
panels.description: Measured from Tanod's side, so it includes the origin's own queueing. Three quantiles on one seconds axis.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Requests waiting for origin capacity. A queue that never empties is latency added to every request rather than capacity being smoothed.

panels.title: Reuse — what is being shared, and what is refused
Cache outcomes
panels.description: hit and stale cost no origin work. bypass is the policy refusing to share a response, which is a correct outcome and not an error.

panels.title: Why a response was not shared
panels.description: A closed set of reasons. Watching which one dominates is how a route that looks cacheable but never is gets diagnosed.

panels.title: Cache occupancy against its budget
panels.description: Both in bytes, one axis. Full is fine; full with a low hit ratio means the working set does not fit and entries are being evicted before they are reused.

panels.title: Spool occupancy against its budget
panels.description: The bounded buffer that lets an origin permit come back when the origin finishes rather than when the client finishes reading.

panels.title: Requests by classification
panels.description: What the classifier decided each request was. static and streaming consume no origin permit by design.

panels.title: Visitors — who was turned away, and was it the site’s own API?
Requests turned away
panels.description: Share of all requests Tanod refused (queue full, queue timeout, or a coalescing wait that ran out) over 5 minutes. Visitors receive these as an error page; on App Platform the 503 arrives as 504.

panels.title: Site API calls turned away
panels.description: The same share for the `api` route only: session, cart, wishlist and other calls the pages make. When these fail, signed-in pages break even if the page itself loaded.

panels.title: Purges (last hour)
panels.description: Invalidations received on the admin listener in the last hour. Content edits in the CMS should show up here; zero during a day of edits means the storefront’s /api/revalidate is not reaching Tanod.

panels.title: Upstream breaker trips (last hour)
panels.description: Times an origin instance was taken out of rotation after failures, in the last hour.

panels.title: Turned away, by route
panels.description: Requests per second refused, per route. A route that sheds while others do not has hit its own concurrency limit, not the global one.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio, by route
panels.description: Share of cacheable requests answered from the cache, per route.

targets.expr: sum by (route) (rate(tanod_cache_total{environment=~"$environment", status=~"hit|stale"}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (route) (rate(tanod_cache_total{environment=~"$environment", status=~"hit|stale|miss"}[5m])), 0.001)

panels.title: Origin instances — is the work spread, and are they all healthy?
Requests per origin instance
panels.description: Origin requests per second, per resolved instance address. The lines should sit together; one carrying everything means the others are not being resolved or are ejected.

panels.title: Work in flight per origin instance
panels.description: Requests each instance is rendering right now.

panels.title: Instance health
panels.description: Healthy (1) and ejected (1) per upstream, plus how many addresses each upstream name resolves to.

panels.title: Telemetry — never load-bearing, still worth watching
Spans
panels.description: dropped means the queue is too small for the traffic; spans are dropped rather than buffered on purpose, because a telemetry queue that grows under load fails during the incident you wanted the traces for. export_failed means the collector is unreachable. Neither ever costs a request.

panels.title: Response spool outcomes
panels.description: budget_exhausted responses fall back to the old behaviour: the permit is held until the client finishes reading, bounded by timeouts.downstream_write.

list.description: Prometheus-compatible data source containing Tanod metrics.
list.label: Metrics data source
list.name: datasource
environment
list.label: Environment
list.description: The environment label the collector stamps on every series (staging, production).
